newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Protexa wins $86 mln Pemex contract - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Protexa wins $86 mln Pemex contract - paper.

text.p: Mexican construction company Protexa Construcciones won the bidding for a $86 million contract to repair marine platforms in the Akal crude oil field, Reforma newspaper reported on Monday.

Protexa's petroleum division manager Domingo Shin Ley said the project will boost state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) crude output by 600,000 barrels per day (bpd), Reforma said. Mexico's crude production in May was 2.99 million bpd.

Construction will begin on August 6 and is due to be finished at the end of 1998, the paper said. Protexa is said to be bidding for other projects in the region, where Pemex has a four-year $4 billion budget for expansion and repairs.
Akal is one of four crude divisions of the lucrative Cantarell field. The contract includes repairs on seven of eight platforms in the region.

"For Protexa Construcciones, these new contracts strengthen the financial structure and the company's payment capacity," he was quoted as saying. Protexa recently placed $90 million in five-year promissory notes as part of a larger $300 million credit program.
Protexa composes about 60 percent of Grupo Protexa, which is planning to go public in 1998.
